name: Vocabulary — starter set
description: General middle/high-school vocabulary, hand-written rather than generated — each word, definition and example sentence checked by a person, the way Word Forge's own built-in bank is.

items.definition: honest and direct, even when the truth is not flattering
items.example: Her candid answer surprised the committee, but they trusted it more for that.

items.definition: extremely careful about every small detail
items.example: He was meticulous about labeling every wire before he unplugged anything.

items.definition: open to more than one interpretation; not clear
items.example: The instructions were ambiguous, so two people set it up two different ways.

items.definition: able to recover quickly after something difficult
items.example: The old laptop was surprisingly resilient — it survived three drops off the desk.

items.definition: based on random choice rather than a reason or system
items.example: The cutoff score felt arbitrary — nobody could explain why it was 70 and not 65.

items.definition: logical and consistent; easy to follow
items.example: Once she reordered the slides, the whole presentation was coherent.

items.definition: showing steady, careful effort over time
items.example: A diligent student reviews notes every day, not just the night before a test.

items.definition: doubting a claim until there is evidence for it
items.example: He stayed skeptical of the ad's promises until he saw the test results.

items.definition: no longer needed because it repeats something already done
items.example: The second backup felt redundant once the first one had been verified.

items.definition: reasonable enough to be believed, even if not proven
items.example: Her explanation for the delay was plausible, so nobody questioned it further.

items.definition: next to or bordering something else
items.example: The battery compartment sits adjacent to the motor, so heat from one affects the other.

items.definition: not favoring one side over another
items.example: A referee has to stay impartial even when the crowd disagrees with a call.

items.definition: able to be touched or clearly grasped; real and concrete
items.example: The prototype gave the team something tangible to react to, instead of just a description.

items.definition: present from birth rather than learned
items.example: Some balance is innate, but most of what looks like natural skill is really practice.

items.definition: using more words than necessary
items.example: The first draft was verbose; cutting it in half made the point land harder.

items.definition: possible to do given the time, tools or resources available
items.example: Printing the part overnight was feasible, but shipping it by morning was not.

items.definition: certain to happen; impossible to avoid
items.example: Once the deadline moved twice, a third delay started to feel inevitable.

items.definition: believable because the source or evidence supports it
items.example: A credible witness described the same sequence of events from a different angle.

items.definition: not obvious; noticed only with close attention
items.example: There was a subtle difference in color between the two batches of filament.

items.definition: general agreement reached by a group
items.example: It took two meetings, but the team finally reached consensus on the layout.
